'Oh Be A Fine Girl/Guy Kiss Me' for OBAFGKM.

walkthroughs.body_html: From hottest to coolest: O B A F G K M. O stars exceed 30,000 K and shine blue; M stars are below 3,700 K and shine red. The Sun is type G2.
Each spectral type has characteristic absorption lines. Hot O stars show ionised helium; cool M stars show molecular bands. The pattern reveals temperature, composition and motion.
lambda_peak * T = 2.9 x 10^-3 m K. A 6,000 K star peaks near 500 nm (yellow-green); cooler stars peak in red and infrared.

mcqs.q: Why are Type Ia supernovae used as 'standard candles'?
options: It is the hottest stage.
They have nearly uniform peak brightness, so their apparent brightness reveals distance.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
Because they happen at regular time intervals.

mcqs.q: What defines a star as being on the 'main sequence'?
options: It is the hottest stage.
It is the largest stage of a star's life.
Because they are the brightest objects in the universe.
It fuses hydrogen into helium in its core.

mcqs.q: What determines whether a star becomes a white dwarf or a neutron star?
options: It is the hottest stage.
Whether it has planets.
Its colour during its main sequence phase.
Its mass - low/medium mass becomes a white dwarf; massive stars produce neutron stars or black holes.
